open_points.subject: content_identity
open_points.text: - content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For every content variant of IdentitySubject (contract_version, implementation, trial_case, flow_version, stored_value, corpus) MUST build one JSON object whose members are exactly the variant's fields keyed by field name, subject_kind included, with nested models as objects keyed by field name, tuples as arrays, enum members as their value text, None as null and JSON-text fields such as value_schema kept as JSON strings, take its canonical bytes with canonical_bytes and return the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of those bytes.
open_points.other_text: - content_identity: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST let NonCanonicalValueError from canonical_bytes propagate unchanged when any JSON text the subject carries cannot be represented canonically; it computes no partial identity.
open_points.question: Must JSON-text fields such as value_schema remain opaque JSON strings, or must their contents be parsed and validated so invalid JSON raises NonCanonicalValueError?

open_points.subject: content_identity idempotency_key variant
open_points.text: - content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For the idempotency_key variant MUST build one JSON object with one member per entry of fields, named by the entry's port and holding the JSON value its canonical_json encodes, so the order of the fields does not change the key, and return the hexadecimal SHA-256 of its canonical bytes; a field whose value is null is kept as null, not dropped.
open_points.other_text: - canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1), which an IEEE double cannot hold exactly, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.
open_points.question: When two fields entries have the same port, must the object contain one member per entry and therefore repeat a member name, or must duplicate ports be rejected or otherwise reconciled before canonical_bytes is called?

open_points.subject: fit_port_value size failure for a cardinality-many value
open_points.text: - fit_port_value: [BEHAVIOR] The size check of a value port compares the length of the candidate's canonical_json, taken as the whole value even for cardinality many, with size_bound and fails when it is larger; size_bound is whatever ceiling the caller passes and the function never chooses one itself.
open_points.other_text: - fit_port_value: [RETURN_SHAPE] Never raises for a candidate that does not fit: returns PortFit with fits true, failed_check None and reason None, or with fits false, failed_check the first failing = models.FitCheck member and a reason naming the port and, for a list, the failing element index.
open_points.question: When the whole cardinality-many JSON value exceeds size_bound, must the reason identify the aggregate value or a failing element index, even though no individual element is tested and an empty array can fail the whole-value size check?

open_points.subject: fit_port_value size-check ordering
open_points.text: - fit_port_value: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] MUST judge the candidate against the port with the checks in exactly this order and stop at the first that fails: presence (candidate is None), carriage, schema, size; within one check the elements of a list are judged in list order and the reason names the index of the first failing element.
open_points.other_text: - fit_port_value: [BEHAVIOR] The size check of a value port compares the length of the candidate's canonical_json, taken as the whole value even for cardinality many, with size_bound and fails when it is larger; size_bound is whatever ceiling the caller passes and the function never chooses one itself.
open_points.question: For a cardinality-many value's size check, must elements be judged in list order with a first failing index, or must only the whole canonical_json byte sequence be judged?

open_points.subject: fit_port_value carriage failure for a file_list candidate
open_points.text: - fit_port_value: [BEHAVIOR] Carriage fits when a port of = models.Carriage value receives a json candidate, a file port of = models.Cardinality one receives a file candidate, and a file port of cardinality many receives a file_list candidate; any other pairing fails the carriage check.
open_points.other_text: - fit_port_value: [RETURN_SHAPE] Never raises for a candidate that does not fit: returns PortFit with fits true, failed_check None and reason None, or with fits false, failed_check the first failing = models.FitCheck member and a reason naming the port and, for a list, the failing element index.
open_points.question: When a file_list candidate fails because its candidate/port pairing is wrong, must the reason name an element index even though carriage is decided for the pairing as a whole and the list may be empty?
